sense.text:
In the Bible a prison is both literal and figurative. Literally it is a place where people were held captive, like Joseph, Jeremiah, John the Baptist and Paul. Figuratively it is spiritual bondage, oppression and slavery: being under the dominion and control of another people or nation, trapped by sin, fear, suffering or disobedience. Deuteronomy 28 shows both.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger”, without food, “and in thirst”, without water, “and in nakedness”, without clothing, “and in want of all things”: and all things includes education, medicine, and religion.

“And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The yokes of iron came off our necks when we were totally destroyed as a people, as a nation, as a race. They literally came off, but they are still on our minds, figuratively, spiritually, mentally. The white man did not release us from slavery until he knew we were mentally destroyed: this people will never unite, this people will never rise up against us. Our people walk around in nice suits and bow ties, go to church and go to work, and think they are free, while the mind is still captive. Jason Whitlock says, I make $10 million a year, I am free, I am not oppressed, I don’t play that victim stuff; Brandon Tatum says the same thing. The results of systemic racism are the proof.

They prove the slavery is still on us mentally, and when it says black people, that includes the Latinos. Low self-esteem and diminished self-worth: the black woman with dead hair on her head, animal hair bought from the Chinese, trying to look like the white woman; the bleaching to change the complexion altogether. They say I love myself. No, you don’t. That is trauma, mental slavery. Internalized racism: in church everything good and holy is white and pure, everything black is evil. Anxiety, depression and hopelessness, brothers and sisters on medication for it. Little Billy who saw a school shooting at Sandy Hook got therapy; we see people killed all the time growing up and suffer generational curses, and where is our therapy? Our only therapy is the Holy Bible.

Hypervigilance, going into a job interview hoping they won’t discriminate for the way you look or wear your hair. Mistrust of the police, schools, healthcare (Edomite doctors who believe black people don’t feel pain the same and give less anesthesia), and government. Identity conflict and shame, identifying with other races before our own; code switching, acting one way among each other and putting on a different voice among Esau. Intergenerational trauma: we think Deuteronomy 28 doesn’t affect us, but it is passed down across whole generations. Sleep problems, stress, high blood pressure, and the collective grief of repeated racial violence.

And it is in full effect today, not only back then: the United States supplies roughly 40% of all the food Jamaica imports, and Trinidad buys about 40% of its imported food from the United States. You thought you were free. You are serving your enemies for your food.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city.” We are not literally dead. This ties in with Deuteronomy 28:48, where the yoke of iron would not come off our necks until we were destroyed: destroyed means dead. We are dead.

The great city is Babylon the great. It is also the valley of dry bones in Ezekiel 37: the valley is Babylon the great, the United States of America, and the dead bodies of the Israelites are those dry bones.

“Which spiritually is called”: that is the key. Not literally, but spiritually, figuratively. “Sodom”, because same-sex marriage is pushed here. “And Egypt”: this is a spiritual Egypt. Look at the dollar bill with the eye of Horus above the pyramid, and the obelisk in Washington DC. This is the spiritual Egypt where the 12 tribes are held captive.

“Where also our Lord was crucified.” Brothers always skip over that part. Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, so this is a spiritual, figurative Jerusalem where our Lord is crucified. How? We don’t want the black Christ who taught the commandments to gather the 12. Kill that. We want the European one who loves everybody and died for everybody.

precepts.why: “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” This is why our dead bodies lie in the street. The white man, the Arabs and the Chinese made sure we would lose our way, lose our identity, lose our self-worth, and forget the laws of God. So we are in the congregation of the dead: dead, not in the body, but as a people who wandered out of the way of understanding.

“Babylon is fallen, is fallen, that great city, because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.” This proves who the great city of Revelation 11:8 is. That great city is Babylon the great, and the dead bodies of our people lie in her streets.

The great city where our dead bodies lie is the valley of dry bones. “The hand of the Lord was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the Lord, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”: this valley full of bones is Babylon the great, the United States of America, and the dry bones are our dead bodies, the dead bodies of the Israelites.

“And, lo, they were very dry.” “Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord God, thou knowest.”

This is what happened when he prophesied to the dry bones. “The sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above”: we started to identify one with another. “But there was no breath in them”: we were not keeping God’s laws at all.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live.” “And the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.” The breath that came into us is the laws of God and the faith of Christ.

“These bones are the whole house of Israel.” Don’t let a Christian fool you and say these are the church people. This is the whole house of Israel, the 12 tribes. “Our bones are dried, and our hope is lost: we are cut off for our parts.”

“Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel.” Are we literally in a grave? No. But we are figuratively dead, in graves. Some of us are in the graveyard called religion: Baptist, Pentecostal, Seventh Day Adventist, Jehovah Witness. Some of us are in the political graves, Republican and Democrat.

“When I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves”: we are in some type of grave. Like all those things we read about systemic racism and the psychological effects, everybody in here has some type of grave. Waking up to the truth that we are the Israelites, we are coming up out of these graves partially, not 100%, because some of us still suffer from depression, fear, mistrust, chronic stress and low self-esteem. A brother who said, I don’t want a sister who don’t have a weave, is still mentally destroyed. Now he is in border, blue and fringes, but the fact that it is in his mind tells us he is still destroyed to a degree.

sense.text:
“We have made a covenant with death”: a covenant means an agreement. The death is the white man and his philosophies. “And with hell are we at agreement”: the hell is our people kept in a low, hellish state. That is how ex-police officer Brandon Tatum can go into Ocean Springs and interview our people, while selling a liquor called Verdict that Amalek helped him produce. That is why Brandon Tatum, Jason Whitlock and Candace Owens say I’m not oppressed, because they make millions, like the ball players and the rappers. You are oppressed, because what they do to the masses of your people they will do to you if you step out of line. Our people join MAGA, the Republican party, the Democratic party.

“When the overflowing scourge shall pass through”, the judgment, “it shall not come unto us”: nothing is going to happen to us, they say. “For we have made lies our refuge”: we have made Christianity our refuge, we have made democracy our refuge. “And under falsehood have we hid ourselves.”

“Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation”: this stone is Christ. “He that believeth shall not make haste”: you will not be confounded. You will be delivered, you will be saved.

“Judgment also will I lay to the line, and righteousness to the plummet: and the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and the waters shall overflow the hiding place.” This is the second coming, the destruction, Armageddon.

Here is what God says to all our people who join with Esau and the Arabs: “And your covenant with death shall be disannulled, and your agreement with hell”, the agreement with our people in a hellish condition, “shall not stand; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, then ye shall be trodden down by it.” God is going to judge them.

precepts.why: Proof of the stone: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. The chief corner stone means he is the leader, the commander. “In whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord.” The tried stone God lays in Zion is Christ.

The same covenant was made back then: “In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen”, an agreement with the other nations, the Greeks in this context, “that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.”

People say the Bible has no relevance today. It has all the relevance in the world. What our people did back then, making a covenant with the Greeks, our people are doing today, making a covenant with every white man or woman they can find. It is the same thing.

“Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces”: you associate yourself with the Democratic party, the Republican party, these Christian denominations, and God said he is going to break you in pieces. That is why everything goes wrong with us in these groups and religions; nothing has gone right in the 62 years since civil rights. “Gird yourselves, and ye shall be broken in pieces.”

“Though hand join in hand”: though you take your little black crusty hand and join it with the hand of society, the white man and the white woman, “the wicked shall not be unpunished.” The white man is still going to get punished, and you are too. “But the seed of the righteous”, who will not join hand in hand with the oppressor, “shall be delivered.”

“Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to the Lord”: that starts with Esau, the proudest nation on the planet. Then you join yourself to him and say, We sick, boss, our house on fire, boss. You associate yourself with him. “Though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.” He is still going to get it, and so are you.

sense.text: Lamentations was written by the prophet Jeremiah. “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” That is the only reason we are all still here. It isn’t due to Martin Luther King Jr., Malcolm X or even H. Rap Brown. It is the Lord’s compassion. “They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” “It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.”

“Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” This is what we as a people often don’t want to do: examine ourselves. To wake up we must start by examining ourselves. What’s wrong with me? Who raised you? Why do you do the things you do? And it is by studying and reading the word of God that we are able to search and try our ways.

“We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned.” That is why we are in the state and condition we are in now. “Thou hast covered with anger, and persecuted us: thou hast slain, thou hast not pitied.”

“Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.” Ex-pastors and ex-Christians ask, Why didn’t God help us during the time of slavery? Verse 42 and verse 44 answer it: we transgressed, and so our prayers did not pass through. That is why the Lord let all that happen to us. But through all of it he did not allow them to destroy us totally.

Sometimes the Lord is not hearing our prayers because of the way we are and the things we do. A pastor prayed and fasted for his niece with brain cancer, she died, and he lost his faith. King David prayed, fasted and cried when God said he would take the child born of Bathsheba, and God still took it. Then David wiped his eyes, washed up and had supper: God made his call. That is how we all have to be, not like these fake Christians who say God killed my mama, so now I hate God, I hate what the Bible says. You are stupid. The souls of our people don’t die.

“Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.” Offscouring is physical dirt, the grime and scum scrubbed off a dirty surface, and a person rejected by society as an outcast. Refuse is waste, doo-doo. That is how they treat us: as scum, trash.

“All our enemies have opened their mouths against us”: the other nations. “Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.” “Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water”: we are crying. “Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission”: there is no stopping, every day is something new. “Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven”: that is what we must wait for, and we must be patient with that. “Mine eye affecteth mine heart”: our crying affects the way we feel.

“They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” A dungeon is prison. Not jail, prison. “And cast a stone upon me”: you are never getting out, you are in there for life. Many black political prisoners are never getting out, not because they committed a crime, but because they were fraudulently held there.

“I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon.” That is all we can do: out of prison, call upon the name of the Lord. “Thou hast heard my voice.” “O Lord, thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul”: only God can plead our cause. “O Lord, thou hast seen my wrong”, my sin: “judge thou my cause.”

“Thou hast seen all their vengeance and all their imaginations against me.” Their vengeance and imaginations against us go all the way back to Cain and Abel: that envy, that jealousy, that hatred. It is the same envy, jealousy and hatred of the time of Jacob and Esau, and it is the same today. “The lips of those that rose up against me, and their device against me all the day.”

“Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their musick.” From the time they sit down, go to sleep and wake up, they are talking about black people. That is why when you move around in their neighborhoods it’s, What are you doing here? What does your t-shirt say? What are your kids doing? The Karens and the male Karens: that is what the verse is talking about.

This is what all of us should be praying. “Render unto them a recompence, O Lord”: judgment, “according to the work of their hands.” “Give them sorrow of heart”: give the nations, give the white man sorrow of heart. “Thy curse unto them. Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord.” That is Bible. The churches are not going to read that, but that is how all of us should feel, with faith in that thing right there.

precepts.why: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” Examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said: “Let us search and try our ways.” Paul says it too: “Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?”

“Now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” Salvation is near, and it is high time we wake up from our sleep. To wake up, we must start by examining ourselves: searching and trying our ways.

“Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law”: I would not know what sin is but by the law. “For I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” So by studying the word of God you are able to examine yourself, to search and try your ways and turn again to the Lord.

sense.text:
Here is a solution, after you repent of your sins; this is what our ancestors did. “And the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers.” It doesn’t say we married them. It doesn’t say we let our sons and daughters play with their kids. “And stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.” That is the solution right there.

Nolan Wells knew the families of the white boys, but their parents said they had never met his. Their families taught them, don’t go over to their house. But it is always blacks and Latinos wanting to be invited to the white folks’ picnic. A father says, I teach my son not to see color. Where the hell you been for the past 400 years? This is still called America. You don’t see color, but color sees you. You stupid or what? That is the stupidest thing I’ve heard. You driving in your car, you see color: red light, green light. Nolan Wells was the only black person in the pool in Mississippi. You better get out of that pool. Remember the four W’s: beware of white folks, water, woods and whiskey, or you are going to end up dead.

precepts.why:
People say separation is not in the New Testament. It is: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord”. It says the same thing as Nehemiah 9:2. There is no contradiction; it is the manipulated mind, raised in Christianity and not taught this, that contradicts the word of God.

God knows you have to work with some of them and sit in school with them; that is not what he is talking about. But after work and after school, when the power is in your hands, you don’t need to go to lunch with them or invite them over to meet your mama and daddy.

“And touch not the unclean thing”: don’t touch their religious doctrines, don’t touch their political doctrines, stay away from them. “And I will receive you”: only then will God receive you, “And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.” You want to be a part of multiculturalism. In school they teach multiculturalism: the white man always on top, black people always on the bottom, and that is what they call equality. We’re all equal as long as white folks, Esau, Edom, is on the top and you are on the bottom, and you at home go along with that.

Even a black evangelical preacher says it: the closer you get to the center of evangelicalism, the further away you have to get from being a black man, and there is an undercurrent of white supremacy in the multiethnic churches that no one wants to talk about. There is still some hope for our brothers and sisters in Christianity, because they know there is something inherently evil in the Christian church. They will learn about every other culture, but when it comes to our people, no, we don’t need to learn about black people.

sense.text:
Righteousness and justice go together. White people should never utter the word justice, because justice condemns them as a race, from the time of Cain until today. They stole this whole country; the schools are built on the blood of our ancestors, Gad, Reuben, even Issachar.

“Thus saith the Lord, Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.”

precepts.why:
“Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins.” “They ask of me the ordinances of justice; they take delight in approaching to God.”

When our people say they want justice, they mean they want money. That is not justice. Justice with the other nations is eye for eye.

An example of God’s justice, read to a Christian woman who said she wanted justice: “He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.” Her shoulders tensed up. That is how Christians are: they say they want justice and believe the Bible, but when you show them the truth of God in the Bible, they hesitate.

“And if a man love righteousness, her labours are virtues: for she teacheth temperance and prudence, justice and fortitude: which are such things, as men can have nothing more profitable in their life.” There is nothing more profitable, nothing more worthwhile in life, brothers and sisters, than righteousness, justice and fortitude.

sense.text:
The Southern Poverty Law Center and the Anti-Defamation League put Israel United in Christ third on their list of America’s largest hate groups, with the Ku Klux Klan at the bottom. “Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer: preserve my life from fear of the enemy. Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked”: this is the secret counsel. We have never burned a cross on anybody’s lawn, never bombed a church and killed four little girls, never dragged anyone with a truck or hung anyone, and they put us on a list, and our own people believe it.

“From the insurrection of the workers of iniquity”: there are conspiracies against us, secret plots against our race.

“Who whet their tongue like a sword”: they speak evil, they manipulate, they are the accusers of the brethren. “And bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words”: bitter words like black-on-black crime. We are the worst thing on the planet, they say. That is a talking point to get black people to shut the f up. Pooky and Ray Ray killing 500 people is still not the genocide Netanyahu is doing, nor what America has committed with its bombs. It don’t compare. Never let black-on-black crime be a talking point to get us to shut up; we are not going to shut up when it comes to genocide. You have murdered millions upon millions of people with your bombings.

“That they may shoot in secret at the perfect”: we are the perfect. Our race is the perfect. No matter how low we are, God says we are the perfect when we repent. “Suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not”: they don’t fear when they shoot those evil words at us.

“They encourage themselves in an evil matter: they commune of laying snares privily”: a snare is a trap; privily means secretly. “They say, Who shall see them?” Who would suspect us? We’re Christians, we’re Jewish, we’re the good guys; you Negroes are the bad guys, nobody will believe you.

precepts.why:
“Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.” That is universal, and Wile E. Coyote always digging a pit or rolling a stone for the Road Runner and falling in it themselves came from the Bible. To the white man digging his pits secretly: you shall fall therein, thus saith the Lord. The stone you roll to fall on our heads will roll back on you.

And it happened: Heidi Beirich, who ran the SPLC’s hate-group tracking and talked about exposing the hypocrisy of the groups, was arrested on fraud charges for secret payments to people inside white supremacist groups, including a one-legged Imperial Wizard of the KKK, and was living with one of them. The splinter group he revived descends from the Klan behind the 16th Street Baptist Church bombing that killed four little girls in 1963. She was funding them. That is why they had us third and the KKK at the bottom. Stop playing with the prophets: when we pray, the Most High brings judgment.

sense.text: “Therefore rejoice, ye heavens”: the heavens are the nations that have nuclear weapons, in particular the so-called Europeans, America and Britain. “And ye that dwell in them.” “Woe”, meaning destruction, “to the inhabiters of the earth”: all the other nations and countries, “and of the sea”: the islands, like Jamaica, Trinidad, Puerto Rico, the Melanesian islands. “For the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.” If you are not part of their heavens, the American and European systems with nuclear weapons (even the Israelis have them), you are the earth and the sea, and the devil is coming down on you.

“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon”: we are talking about Babylon. “How hath the oppressor ceased!” Babylon is an oppressive country, an oppressive system. “The golden city ceased!” Golden city means rich beyond belief. If you believe America has a deficit and owes everybody money, you are foolish; God calls this place the golden city, and they print their own money.

“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!” God is calling Babylon the great Lucifer. He has not changed the subject, only the metaphor: Babylon and Lucifer are the same. “How art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” Compare the oppressor of verse 4 with “which didst weaken the nations” here. They weaken the nations through oppression and economically: they control the international monetary funding, the World Bank, and say Africa’s and Jamaica’s money is worthless. The United States supplies roughly 40% of all Jamaica’s imported food, and Trinidad buys about 40% of its imported food from the United States. That is Deuteronomy 28:48 in full effect today.

“For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”: that is space travel. “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation”: that is slavery. When you sit on somebody, you have conquered them. The congregation is Israel. “In the sides of the north”: that is North America.
“I will ascend above the heights of the clouds”: airplanes, helicopters. “I will be like the most High”: I will be like God.
“Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit.” Regardless of all the technological power you have, America, Babylon, Lucifer, you are going to be brought down to hell.

“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man”: so Lucifer is a man on earth. What man? The white man. “That made the earth to tremble, that did shake kingdoms”: in 2016, the final year of Obama’s presidency, the United States dropped an estimated 26,171 bombs on seven countries, about 72 a day, three every hour, killing thousands of civilians that year alone. Trump has struck ten countries. Pooky and Ray Ray never did devastation like this. Don’t ever let them use that talking point about black-on-black crime compared to this. They better shut their pink lips. The capture of Maduro in Venezuela, the oil blockade that cut Cuba off and brought it to the verge of humanitarian collapse, the pressure on countries to end Cuba’s doctor programs, the bombing of Iran: what we see in the news is what we read in Isaiah 14. And you can’t have the oppressor investigate himself; he will always give a low number.

“That made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed the cities thereof”: that is what Obama did and what Trump is doing. “That opened not the house of his prisoners?” This is what the lesson is about. We are the prisoners, though our people believe they are not slaves and believe they are free. As H. Rap Brown said, what better way to enslave a people than to give them the vote and make them think they’re free. The captives are here, the congregation he sits upon in the sides of the north.

The political prisoners are in the house he will not open: H. Rap Brown, Imam Jamil Al-Amin, sentenced to life and kept in solitary confinement for 20-plus years while another man confessed to the crime again and again; Mumia Abu-Jamal, the MOVE members, the former Black Panthers and Black Liberation Army members, many held for four decades, many not allowed visitors, nearly all convicted of the same crime.

precepts.why: Who is the congregation? Is it the church, the Baptist church, the Catholic church? “Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.” The congregation is the people God purchased of old, Mount Zion.

“All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.” That settles it: the congregation is Israel. So “the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north” is Israel, sat upon and conquered in North America.

sense.text:
“Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise”: the brethren are the 11 tribes. “Thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies”: that is why the political prisoners were shown. Judah has been fighting this white man from the beginning, always struggling for independence, always fighting, and not for no reason, but for the liberation of his people.

“Thy father’s children shall bow down before thee”: because Judah would be in the forefront, teaching and gathering the tribes.

“Judah is a lion’s whelp”: the tribe of Judah is like a young lion, powerful. “From the prey, my son, thou art gone up”: Judah went up from going after the prey, which is the nations. “He stooped down”, as if about to pounce, “he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?” What happened? They gave us crack, heroin, feminism, bad education, and Judah rolled over and went to sleep. Now we just want money; the fight is gone. But the true liberation comes from the teachers of the Bible.

precepts.why:
“And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people”. Judah would be the one going out to find the tribes and teach them the word of God. So not only would Judah be fighting in the system he lives in; a remnant would wake up, go out, teach, and bring the 12 tribes of Israel. That is why “thy father’s children shall bow down before thee.”

Read again at the end of the deliverance scriptures: “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah”: Judah would be the ones in the street fighting for liberation and salvation. “And bring him unto his people”: help him find and teach the tribes. “Let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies”: help Judah against his enemies, against the white man. That is the prophecy.

sense.text: More about Judah, whose hand is in the neck of his enemies. “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north”: the north is North America. “For I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven”: we are scattered everywhere.

“Deliver thyself, O Zion”: Zion here is Judah. Deliver thyself, O Judah, “that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon”: that is, with the so-called Caucasians, here in North America. The question is how we deliver ourselves, and Revelation 18 answers it.

precepts.why: To show that Zion in Zechariah 2:7 is Judah: “But chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” Judah is the mount Zion which he loved.

Who is the daughter of Babylon? “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof. O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”. Edom, which means red, the red people, is called the daughter of Babylon. So Judah dwelling with the daughter of Babylon is Judah dwelling with Edom, the so-called Caucasians, here in North America.

This is how we deliver ourselves: “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins”. Not being partakers in the sins of America: not taking part in their religious ceremonies and denominations, their political groups and traditions. “And that ye receive not of her plagues”: it says the same thing as 2 Corinthians 6:17, come out from among them.

“For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.” America’s sins have reached unto heaven. “Reward her even as she rewarded you”: and the you is the tribes of Israel. “And double unto her double according to her works”: America is going to get double what they did to us.

sense.text: “For Israel hath not been forsaken, nor Judah of his God, of the Lord of hosts”: it may look like we have been forsaken, but the Bible prophesies we have not. “Though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel.” Look at our people right now: in a low state, destitute, degenerate as a race. That is how it is put out there: the twerkers, the drug dealers, the homeless. But God said, regardless of all that, I have not forsaken them.

“Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and deliver every man his soul”: the way you flee is to deliver your soul, and the way you deliver your soul is through repentance and keeping God’s commandments. “Be not cut off in her iniquity”: the same thing Revelation 18 says. “For this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance; he will render unto her a recompence.”

precepts.why: “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel”. Why does it say yet choose? Look at us. We went into slavery because of our sins and are still in a degenerate condition. Regardless of all that, the pimps and the hoes, the drug dealers, the baby mama drama, whatever names you have for us, God said, I will yet choose them. He is not casting off his chosen people. There is still hope. It says the same thing as “Israel hath not been forsaken.”

“The righteous cry, and the Lord heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.” That is what happened in ancient Egypt, and it is going to happen again today. “The Lord is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.” “Many are the afflictions of the righteous”: that is why we go through all these ups and downs and turmoil. “But the Lord delivereth him out of them all.”

“And the Lord shall help them, and deliver them: he shall deliver them from the wicked, and save them, because they trust in him.” The key to salvation is trusting in the one true God, trusting in our king.
“Judge me, O God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation”: the white man, America, Europe is the ungodly nation. “O deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man.”
“Deliver me from mine enemies, O my God: defend me from them that rise up against me.”

sense.text:
In Planet of the Apes (whose author based the original on the Watts riots in LA, a metaphor for black people) Caesar opens the cage of the big silverback gorilla who has been locked up for years. The cage is open, but he stops at the line and backs up, until at last he comes out. That is black people: we say we are free and the cage is open, but the chain is still on our minds and we will not go past what society says we can do. Our men in Mississippi are broken, mentally destroyed. So we use the word of God to break the chains of oppression from the minds of our people.

“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek”: the Lord has given us the power through his word to preach the good news unto the meek. “He hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted”: many of our brothers and sisters see the public lynching of our people and are brokenhearted, and God has anointed us with the spirit of his word to bind them up, those who feel they can’t go past that bound even with the cage door open.

“To proclaim liberty to the captives”: freedom to those in cages like the gorilla. The mind is caged, enclosed, and the spirit of God is on us to preach freedom to those bound in mental cages. “And the opening of the prison to them that are bound”: we just saw the opening of the prison in that example.

We might think Christ doesn’t understand what we are going through. He knows perfectly well. The whole chapter is about Christ. “He was taken from prison and from judgment”: from Pilate’s judgment seat. “And who shall declare his generation?” We shall: the seed that serves him. “For he was cut off out of the land of the living”: that is when he was crucified. “For the transgression of my people was he stricken.”

precepts.why: How he was taken from judgment: “And from thenceforth Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Cesar’s friend”. Pilate “brought Jesus forth, and sat down in the judgment seat in a place that is called the Pavement, but in the Hebrew, Gabbatha.” They cried, “Away with him, away with him, crucify him.” “The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cesar. Then delivered he him therefore unto them to be crucified. And they took Jesus, and led him away.”

Who shall declare his generation? “A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation. They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness”: to declare means to teach, to preach. That is us, you and me, “unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done this.”

Cut off out of the land of the living: “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”. The Messiah is Christ, and he didn’t die for himself. “And the people of the prince that shall come”, Rome, “shall destroy the city and the sanctuary; and the end thereof shall be with a flood, and unto the end of the war desolations are determined.”

“And they watched him, and sent forth spies, which should feign themselves just men, that they might take hold of his words”: that is the SPLC and the ADL today. “That so they might deliver him unto the power and authority of the governor.”

So be mindful, brothers, of the things you say and do. The person sitting next to you may be getting paid to listen and set brothers and sisters up, like the man in New York who wanted us to buy weapons.

“And like as a spy, watcheth he for thy fall”: he watches for your demise. “For he lieth in wait, and turneth good into evil, and in things worthy praise will lay blame upon thee.” The good things you say, he or she will turn into evil. That is what the Pharisees did with Christ: all the good he taught, they said he was going to overthrow Rome and destroy the temple.

“Take heed of a mischievous man, for he worketh wickedness”. “Receive a stranger into thine house, and he will disturb thee, and turn thee out of thine own.” Brothers invite people over to learn the scriptures, and that is fine, but be careful: you don’t know all these brothers, their wives or their kids, only that his name is Shabazz or Hakeem, and you bring him around your wife and children. And bringing a brother the host doesn’t know into another brother’s house is evil as hell and stupid as hell. Y’all got to be wiser than that. Wait until you get to know him.

sense.text: “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”: because all the promises pertain to the Israelites. “And I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not”: that is Netanyahu and his people; they are not the biblical Jews. “But are the synagogue of Satan”: Christ called them the synagogue of Satan.

“Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”: he goes from calling them the synagogue of Satan to the devil, one and the same. In that time it was Herod, a converted Jew. “That ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death”.

When you read of Peter locked up and the angel coming to save him, that is not the lot for all of us. Some of us will have the lot of this verse: Christ is not coming to save you from it, just as he didn’t save John the Baptist. Be faithful unto death. We must mentally prepare ourselves for what is to come. “And I will give thee a crown of life”: death is not the end. The body being finished does not mean the spirit and soul are finished.

“The whole earth is at rest, and is quiet”: when this white man goes down, the whole earth will be at rest and quiet. “They break forth into singing”: the whole earth will break forth into singing and rejoicing.

“I the Lord have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand”: brothers and sisters, he has called us all in righteousness, and he will hold our hand. “And will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people”: Christ is the covenant of the people. “For a light of the Gentiles”: the Gentiles are the northern kingdom.

“To open the blind eyes”: we are the blind eyes. Our people think they see, think they are woke, and they don’t see or understand. “To bring out the prisoners from the prison”: our people are the prisoners to be brought out. Just because you can’t see the bars does not mean you are not in prison, with your low self-esteem, hating yourself and hating your people. That is a prison house. “And them that sit in darkness”: we sit in darkness and think this is bright and light. “Out of the prison house”: we are the people in the prison house.

“But this is a people robbed and spoiled; they are all of them snared in holes”: we are all trapped, snared in holes. “And they are hid in prison houses”: whether the prison house is democracy, Republicans, socialism, liberals, Baptists or Episcopal, these are all prison houses. “They are for a prey, and none delivereth”: nobody delivers us. “For a spoil, and none saith, Restore”: none of the nations say restore to us.

precepts.why: “That thou mayest say to the prisoners, Go forth; to them that are in darkness, Shew yourselves.” This is the message we have for our people, because our people are the prisoners. It is what Caesar said to the big gorilla in the film: go forth, come out of that cage. “They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places”: that is the kingdom.

“For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust”: he died for us; he was the just and we are the unjust, “that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened”, changed, “by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison”.

We are the spirits in prison that he preached to. Christians talk about him going under the ground. No: being dominated by another race is a prison. Christ came to us while Rome dominated us, and he preached to us.

This is about the ancient Egyptians in the plague of darkness, and it relates to us: “So then whosoever there fell down was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars”. Just like the Egyptians in that sea of darkness, that is what we are in today: a prison without iron bars. People say I’m free, there are no shackles on me. There are no iron bars, and it is the same thing.

sense.text: “As for thee also, by the blood of thy covenant”: that is Christ dying on the cross. “I have sent forth thy prisoners”: that is you and me, “out of the pit”: the pit is Babylon, “wherein is no water”: no truth is taught here except what we are teaching.

“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: we are the prisoners of hope, and the stronghold is the commandments in the name of Christ. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”.

“When I have bent Judah for me”: God is going to bend the tribe of Judah to his will. “Filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion”: he raises up the other ten tribes, “against thy sons, O Greece”: against Esau, Edom, the so-called white man. “And made thee as the sword of a mighty man”: God is going to transform us into the sword of a mighty man; he is going to give us power.

“And the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south”: the chariots of God. “The Lord of hosts shall defend them; and they shall devour”: we shall devour the nations, “and subdue with sling stones; and they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine”: we are going to party like we have never partied before.

“And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people”: he is not saving all nations, only the 12 tribes. “For they shall be as the stones of a crown, lifted up as an ensign upon his land.” “For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! corn shall make the young men cheerful, and new wine the maids.”
